title: Cross-tenant snapshot exports: intake taxonomy, SLA lanes, and prioritization rubric
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Enterprise customers frequently request scheduled, full-tenant or cross-tenant snapshot exports for billing audits, regulatory snapshotting, and internal analytics. Current intake is ad-hoc (support tickets + bespoke engineering work). This ticket defines a repeatable intake taxonomy, SLA lanes, prioritization rubric, and concrete deliverables (API contract, console flow, cost estimator) so we can productize scheduled snapshot exports and reduce manual triage work.

Goals: 
- Create a clear taxonomy that maps request types to delivery paths: self-serve template, queued scheduled export (standard), queued scheduled export (premium), and concierge delivery.
- Define priority lanes and SLA expectations for each lane (latency, retry windows, error budgets, cost ceilings).
- Produce a prioritization rubric for PMs/Support that scores requests on business impact, regulatory need, data residency complexity, cost-sensitivity, and readiness for self-serve.
- Deliver minimal API schema + console UX mocks and an export manifest contract that engineering can implement as a single worker pattern.

Constraints & non-goals: 
- This is intentionally scoped to non-bug feature work (no immediate incident remediation).
- Does not include on-prem agent or private-deploy installation packaging (those will be separate epics).
- Cost model decisions will be pragmatic: surface estimated compute/egress cost in intake but do not finalize billing productization here.

Why different from existing export playbooks: 
- Focus is cross-tenant and scheduled snapshots (not ad-hoc one-off exports or dashboards).
- Emphasis on triage rubric for operational teams to reduce manual engineering involvement for repeatable requests.

decision_log: Prefer a 4-lane taxonomy (self-serve, standard queued, premium queued, concierge) instead of a binary self-serve/hand-off model to reduce churn.
Route high-cost or long-running exports into a premium queued lane with a cost-estimate commitment to customer before execution.
Use a manifest-based worker (JSON schema) to decouple console intake from execution and enable retries, checkpointing, and resumable exports.
Surface an estimated cost and estimated wall time during intake; do not finalize billing changes in this ticket—only informational.
All PII or regulator-triggered exports require additional legal signoff and cannot be self-serve without explicit safeguards.
